answer_text: This topic connects closely to broader ideas about how democracies function. In a democracy, the judiciary serves as an independent branch responsible for interpreting and applying the law, as well as ensuring that legislation and executive actions remain within the bounds set by the constitution. One key function is judicial review, where courts can examine whether a law passed by the legislature is constitutional, and strike it down if it is not. Debates about this kind of institution come up regularly in public discussion.
